analysis.title: GS Novak - GS U.S. Industrials & Materials | another big day
key_insights: US S&P futures were little changed in the pre-market on 10/28. Headlines on geopolitical events were driving the tape, including Netanyahu overtaking Eisenkot in the polls with half the vote counted.
Fears of Middle East re-escalation around and after the US midterms continue to lift crude. WTI is about $102 and Brent about $115, up 2%.
The Fed is due to speak today (FOMC). The desk expects a hold. The debate is over the details and what the market will price for December afterwards.
KOSPI spiked overnight, up 663bps, which the desk reads as evidence of risk-on across markets. A SK Hynix profit surge helped lift sentiment.
AI/data center industrials report pre-market. Hyperscalers including MSFT and GOOG are important to watch post-market.
The 10-year yield is firm and very slightly above 5%. The dollar is bid in tandem with DXY above 102. Bitcoin is up 100bps to $81.3k. Precious metals are moving opposite to crude.
Crop prices continue to languish, with corn below $4.50.
Europe is flattish as French unrest calms. The macro data to watch today are the trade balance and retail inventories.

European earnings reads: 8TRA GR -1% on a Q3 miss, with orders, sales and EBIT all missing and guidance unchanged while consensus already sits above the midpoint. FER SM -1% on a beat from better mix, driven by construction rather than roads. KNEBV FH -4% on a Q3 miss with guidance unchanged and orders in line. DSY FP -2% despite better sales and M&A driving a guidance raise. SGO FP -1% after in-line organic growth, with Americas in line against low expectations. STLAM IM +4% on a revenue and EBIT beat, reaffirmed guidance and an expectation of positive industrial free cash flow in 2027.
GPI Q3 EPS of $9.36 came in below the $9.5 consensus on lower revenue of $5.4bn vs $5.58bn. GPI acquired 14 dealerships year to date with about $2bn of expected annual revenue.

AOS will sell an 81% interest in AO Smith China to CPE, valuing the business at $400mm cash-free and debt-free. AOS retains 10% and enters a long-term brand licensing agreement. Closing is expected in 1H'27.
